title: A comprehensive method for quantifying human cytomegalovirus plaque assays
author: Kelnhofer-Millevolte, Laurel E.
materials: We recommend using six-well plates rather than 12-well plates for hCMV plaque assays because they result in less variation between wells. Furthermore, we recommend at least three serial dilutions per condition to be tested in triplicate as described below. We have listed an example of an infection below, with the Towne strain on HFF-T cells which require DMEM. Adjust the cell line and media according to Table 1 depending on the hCMV strain.
Proceed to image processing in Section 3.7.
Imaging option 2—Bio-Rad ChemiDoc™ MP Imaging System:

For images acquired on Bio-Rad ChemiDoc™ MP imaging system or smartphone, use the line tool to trace 1 cm along the top edge of the ruler. Then, in the “Analyze” tab, select “Set Scale”. The length of the traced line will auto-populate in pixels. Ensure that “Known distance” is set to 1 and “Unit of length” is set to cm. Select “OK” to confirm scale.

Adjust the contrast and brightness of the image so that the diagonal contrast line is just touching the edge of the side of peak on confocal images (Figure 3A) the top of the singular peak in Bio-Rad Chemdoc™ images (Figure 3B), or positioned immediately after the first of the two peaks in the smartphone images (Figure 3C). This is done by selecting the “Image” tab and then selecting the “Adjust” tab.

Example histograms indicating how to apply the threshold. (A) Example histogram of contrast from confocal imaging with a diagonal line illustrating how to adjust contrast to the base of the curve. (B) Example histogram of contrast from Bio-Rad imager with a diagonal line illustrating how to adjust contrast to the peak of the curve. (C) Example histogram of contrast from smartphone imaging with a diagonal line illustrating how to adjust contrast to the middle of the bimodal curves. (D) Example positioning of threshold level.

steps.title: Define experimental layout
steps.instruction: Plate the experiment as desired (e.g., siRNA or inhibitor treatment) following the referenced methods.

steps.title: Infect cells with virus
steps.instruction: Dilute the virus in serum‑free media to the desired MOI (the authors use MOI = 1). Add the inoculum to the cells, incubate 1 h with shaking every 10 min (use a rocker or hand‑rock the plates). After 1 h replace the inoculum with media containing 4 % FBS (recipe in Section 6.4, Table 2). For the Towne strain harvest supernatant between 4 and 6 days post‑infection.

steps.title: Harvest and freeze supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect the supernatant into 15‑mL centrifuge tubes (use multiple 15‑mL or 50‑mL tubes for larger volumes). Centrifuge at 3 000 g for 2 min to remove debris. Aliquot 1 mL portions into cryovials or microcentrifuge tubes. Flash‑freeze the aliquots in liquid nitrogen (or a dry‑ice/100 % ethanol slurry) and store at –80 °C or proceed directly to dilution.

steps.title: Prepare HFF‑T cells (Day 0)
steps.instruction: Treat HFF‑T cells with trypsin, harvest, count, and plate them for infection.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate media, wash twice with 10 mL 1× PBS (aspirate after each wash).
Add 3 mL trypsin, incubate 37 °C for 5–10 min.
Add 9 mL DMEM + 10 % FBS, gently triturate to detach cells, transfer to a 15‑mL tube.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min.
Aspirate supernatant carefully, resuspend pellet in 10 mL DMEM + 10 % FBS.
Count cells (fibroblasts) with a hemocytometer.
Dilute to ~210 000 cells per 2 mL using DMEM + 10 % FBS.
Plate 2 mL of the cell suspension per well of a six‑well plate, shaking the plate along X and Y axes to distribute cells evenly.
Incubate plates overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Check confluence and plan dilutions
steps.instruction: Verify that the Day 0 plates are 100 % confluent before proceeding. Do not thaw virus until cells are ready. Recommended viral dilutions for the Towne strain: 10⁻² to 10⁻⁴ for high‑MOI experiments (MOI 1–3) and undiluted to 10⁻² for low‑MOI experiments (MOI 0.1–0).

steps.title: Thaw and sonicate viral stock (Day 1)
steps.instruction: Thaw the viral aliquot (unknown titer) in a 37 °C water bath. If the aliquot is a stock for a plaque assay, sonicate briefly: 1 min on, 1 min off, 1 min on.

steps.title: Prepare dilution series
steps.instruction: Create serial dilutions of the virus in serum‑free DMEM.

substeps.instruction: Label microcentrifuge and 15‑mL tubes with the intended dilution (e.g., 10⁻¹, 10⁻², …).
Add 3.6 mL serum‑free DMEM to each tube (for the 10⁻¹ tube start with 900 µL DMEM).
Vortex the viral aliquot for 30 s, then pipet up/down ≥5 times to coat the tip.
Transfer 100 µL of the viral supernatant into the 10⁻¹ tube, discard the tip.
Vortex the 10⁻¹ tube for 30 s and triturate three times with a fresh tip.
Transfer 400 µL from the 10⁻¹ tube into the next dilution tube, discard the tip.
Repeat the vortex‑transfer‑vortex steps until the desired final dilution is reached (Figure 2).

steps.title: Wash plates and add inoculum
steps.instruction: Prepare the six‑well plates for infection.

substeps.instruction: Remove plates from the incubator, aspirate media.
Wash each well with 1 mL PBS, aspirate PBS (do not disturb the monolayer).
Vortex each dilution tube for 10 s.
Immediately add 1 mL of the corresponding dilution to each well; dispense each dilution into three separate wells.

steps.title: Incubate plates with agitation
steps.instruction: Incubate the inoculated plates for 1 h, agitating the plates every 10 min to ensure even viral coating.

steps.title: Overnight incubation with inoculum
steps.instruction: Leave the plates with inoculum on the cells overnight (≈16–18 h) at 37 °C.

steps.title: Prepare methylcellulose overlay (Day 2)
steps.instruction: Make the overlay that will be added after the overnight infection.

substeps.instruction: In a 50‑mL centrifuge tube, pour ~15 mL of 2 % methylcellulose (Section 6.1).
Gently pipette 15 mL DMEM + 4 % FBS on top of the methylcellulose.
Warm the overlay in a 37 °C water bath for at least 30 min.
Gently triturate the warmed overlay several times, avoiding bubbles.

steps.title: Apply overlay and add DMEM mid‑incubation
steps.instruction: Overlay the infected monolayers and add supplemental media halfway through the extended incubation.

substeps.instruction: Remove plates from incubator, aspirate inoculum (use a fresh tip for each dilution).
Wash each well with 1 mL 1× PBS, aspirate PBS.
Pipet 2 mL of the methylcellulose‑based overlay into each well slowly, supporting the tip on the well edge to minimise bubbles.
Halfway through the extended incubation (≈7 days), gently layer an additional 1 mL warmed DMEM + 4 % FBS onto each well.

steps.title: Monitor plaque development
steps.instruction: Inspect plaque size daily from days 10–14. For the Towne strain plaques are typically ready to fix at day 14; adjust according to Table 1 for other strains.

steps.title: Remove overlay and add PBS (Day 14)
steps.instruction: Begin the fixation and staining procedure.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate approximately half of the overlay by tilting the plate to ~60° and aspirating from the side of the well.
Add 1 mL 1× PBS to each well, layering on top of the remaining overlay.
Aspirate half of the PBS/inoculum using the same tilting method.
Repeat the aspirate‑add‑aspirate cycle two more times (total three washes) until the overlay is clear.

steps.title: Stain plaques with crystal violet
steps.instruction: Fix and stain the plaques for visualization.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL of 1 % crystal violet (Section 6.2) to each well.
Gently shake the plates and place them on a low‑speed orbital shaker at room temperature for 15 min.
Remove most of the crystal violet by flipping the six‑well plate over a funnel into a waste container; tap until splatter stops.
If needed, wash the wells with deionized water using a pipette and collect the waste in a disposal canister.

steps.title: Wash, dry, and prepare plates for imaging
steps.instruction: Finalize the plates before imaging.

substeps.instruction: Dunk the plate right‑side‑up repeatedly in a tub of deionized water until plaques contrast clearly against the monolayer.
Place the plates upside‑down on a bench pad, leaning against the lid, and let them dry overnight.

steps.title: Image plaques – confocal microscope
steps.instruction: Acquire high‑content fluorescence images using a confocal system.

substeps.instruction: Place the fixed plates (plastic bottoms facing the objective, no lid) in the microscope holder (e.g., Zeiss LSM 980).
Set acquisition to Cy5 (647 nm excitation) with a 10× objective and collect fluorescence images.
Open the acquisition tab, select “AI Sample Finder”, choose “Center Position” and click “Find Sample” to generate ROIs for each well.
Configure tile viewer: Tiles → Show viewer → Setup from sample carrier.
Set Fill Factor to 100 % and select all wells (+).
Set tile size to 850.1 µm × 709.3 µm and tile overlap to 10 %.
Add support points: Tiles → Focus Surface and Support Points → Multiple Support Points → 4 columns × 4 rows → Distribute → Interpolation Degree = 2 (Parabolic Saddle Surface).
Live → Verify Support Points; verify each point, using “Set Z and move to next”.
Tile acquisition options: Tile Overlap = 10 %; Travel = meander; Tile Regions/Positions = Sort by Y, then X; Carrier Wells/Container = Meander.
Start the experiment.

Stitching: Processing → Geometric → Stitching → Parameters = Inplace; Channels = All Individually; Edge detector = yes; Minimal Overlap = 5 %; Max Shift = 10 %; Optimized for Comparer; Best for Global Optimizer. Select the newly generated tiled image as input.
Split scenes: Processing → Utilities → Split Scenes → Input the stitched image → choose output folder → Apply.
Export the split files as .czi.
Import .czi into ImageJ via Plugins → Bio‑Formats Importer; check “Use virtual stack”, open the last scene.
Convert to 8‑bit: Image → Type → 8‑bit.
Add a scalebar: Analyze → Tools → Scalebar…, set desired size.
Save as JPEG: File → Save As → JPEG.

steps.title: Image plaques – ChemiDoc MP
steps.instruction: Capture fluorescence images with a Bio‑Rad ChemiDoc™ MP system.

substeps.instruction: Place the fixed plates right‑side‑up (no lid) on the black background plate of the ChemiDoc.
Position a fluorescent metric ruler along the edge of the six‑well plate.
Select the Cy5.5 imaging channel and set exposure to 1–2 s (or use auto‑exposure).
Collect the image.

steps.title: Image plaques – smartphone
steps.instruction: Use a smartphone camera to photograph the stained plaques.

substeps.instruction: Lay a sheet of white paper on a benchtop (or use a light box).
Place the fixed plates upside‑down on the paper.
If desired, place a metric ruler along the plate edge.
Hold the smartphone parallel to the well, tap to focus, avoid casting shadows.
Capture the image and, if necessary, convert the file to .jpg.

steps.title: Process images in ImageJ
steps.instruction: Prepare images for quantitative analysis.

substeps.instruction: Open the image file in ImageJ and ensure it is 8‑bit (Image → Type → 8‑bit).
Set the spatial scale: use the line tool to trace 1 cm on the ruler, then Analyze → Set Scale, Known distance = 1, Unit of length = cm, OK.
Outline the well of interest with the circle drawing tool.

Adjust contrast/brightness (Image → Adjust → Brightness/Contrast) until the diagonal contrast line touches the appropriate feature (diagonal line for confocal, peak for ChemiDoc, middle of bimodal curve for smartphone).
Apply a 1.5 % Gaussian blur (Process → Filters → Gaussian Blur, sigma set to achieve ~1.5 %).
Adjust the threshold (Image → Adjust → Threshold) to include approximately 2.5 %–5 % of pixels; use the mask preview to ensure plaques are covered.
Fill holes (Process → Binary → Fill Holes).
Analyze particles (Analyze → Analyze Particles), setting a lower size limit appropriate to exclude background noise.

steps.title: Analyze plaques and export data
steps.instruction: Obtain plaque counts and sizes and save the results.

substeps.instruction: Export the particle analysis results to Excel or another data‑processing program (File → Save As → .xls/.csv).
Repeat the entire image‑processing workflow for all collected images using the same parameters.
